newsitem.title: ITALY: Hard-left to back Italy govt in any confidence vote.
newsitem.headline: Hard-left to back Italy govt in any confidence vote.

text.p: Italy's hard-left Communist Refoundation, a key ally of Prime Minister Romano Prodi, is ready to back the government in any confidence test after a vote on a security force for Albania, news agency AGI said on Wednesday.

It quoted Refoundation leader Fausto Bertinotti as saying he opposed the mission but would not bring down the government. The Italian-led force has caused political turmoil, sparked by Refoundation's refusal of support. The report could not immediately be confirmed.
Bertinotti later confirmed to reporters at the Chamber of Deputies (lower house) that his party would vote with the centre-left government in any subsequent confidence motion.
"If the government calls a confidence vote that has nothing to do with the Albania mission, then we'll vote 'yes,'" he said.
"It's absolutely obvious...our position is still 'no' regarding the mission but we would say 'yes' to anything that has to do with guaranteeing the continuity of the government."
Newspapers said Prodi would offer to resign in exchange for a deal with the centre-right opposition on the force. The Chamber of Deputies (lower house) is due to vote on the force later on Wednesday.
